answer: No, don't build a record-at-a-time path by default. Source: lesson pa_pattern_batch_or_stream_intermediate.md, section 'Micro-batch or True Streaming?'. The 3-minute SLA is the decider. Check it against the engine's latency floor: trigger plus run, with p99 under the SLA. A micro-batch with a trigger of roughly 10-30 seconds (p99 about 40 s) fits easily under 3 minutes. Then the team decides. Your operations group already runs the batch engine, so micro-batch on that existing cluster, with the same code, deploy pipeline and on-call rotation, wins. Record-at-a-time only pays off when the SLA is shorter than any micro-batch floor, such as sub-second or 2-second needs.
